The new 4 modes are:
1. CSR mode (profiles a kernel; boundary = csrwi 0x7C0,0/1 markers in source)
2. PC mode (profiles a kernel; boundary = PC/symbol address)
3. icount mode (profiles a sampled window; N insts QEMU fast-forward, M insts vsim warmup unrecorded, T insts vsim measured)
4. SimPoint-driven mode (profiles the whole program; clustering picks representative slices, each measured like icount mode)

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (M1..M8) and run one round-trip end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, or instruction count)
21	hands control between them. One run is three legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim  -- same files -->  QEMU2
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)         (fast)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./hsim`
35	
36	`./hsim` is the canonical end-user entry point. It wraps the
37	developer-grade scripts documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`,
38	`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind four subcommands.
39	
40	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
41	
42	```sh
43	./hsim build                                            # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
44	./hsim list fixtures                                    # discover available fixtures
45	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr     # one CSR-mode round-trip
46	./hsim test                                             # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
47	```
48	
49	Expected last line of `./hsim test`:
50	
51	```
52	PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
53	```
54	
55	Subcommand cheat sheet:
56	
57	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
58	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
59	| `./hsim list <fixtures|demos|modes>`                             | List available fixtures, demos, or trigger modes (M1..M8).          |
60	| `./hsim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                       | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`. |
61	| `./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc|icount|slice [-v]`               | Run one ELF through the QEMU -> vsim -> QEMU round-trip.            |
62	| `./hsim test [--filter REGEX] [--mode csr|pc|both] [--jobs N]`   | Run the e2e suite; defaults `--mode both --jobs 8`.                 |
63	
64	Run `./hsim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand. The rest
65	of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the underlying scripts and is
66	useful when you need to bypass `./hsim` (custom env vars, single-leg
67	debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 1. Build and environment setup
72	
73	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
74	
75	Install these on the host once:
76	
77	| Package          | Notes                                                |
78	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
79	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
80	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
81	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
82	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
83	| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests, demo scripts             |
84	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
85	| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
86	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
87	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
88	| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
89	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
90	
91	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
92	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
93	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
94	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
95	
96	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
97	
98	```sh
99	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
100	cd hybrid_sim
101	```
102	
103	If you forgot `--recursive`:
104	
105	```sh
106	git submodule update --init --recursive
107	```
108	
109	Submodules under this repo:
110	
111	| Path             | What it is                                          |
112	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
113	| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
114	| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
115	| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |
116	
117	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
118	
119	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
120	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
121	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
122	
123	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
124	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
125	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
126	`config.env`:
127	
128	```sh
129	# config.env
130	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
131	```
132	
133	The single variable today is:
134	
135	| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
136	|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
137	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
138	
139	How it propagates:
140	
141	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
142	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
143	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
144	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
145	  the variable is missing.
146	- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
147	  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
148	  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.
149	
150	Override per-invocation without editing the file:
151	
152	```sh
153	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
154	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain bash tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh
155	```
156	
157	### 1.4 Build everything
158	
159	One command builds all four artifacts and exports the env vars the
160	test harness expects:
161	
162	```sh
163	source ./setup.sh
164	```
165	
166	`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
167	dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN`,
168	`SIMPOINT_BIN`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
169	runs:
170	
171	```
172	0/4 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
173	                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
174	1/4 QEMU       -> build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
175	2/4 vsim       -> verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium    (in container)
176	3/4 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
177	4/4 SimPoint   -> tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
178	```
179	
180	To rebuild just one component:
181	
182	```sh
183	./scripts/build_qemu.sh
184	./scripts/build_vsim.sh        # uses podman + Dockerfile (target `env`)
185	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU
186	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh
187	```
188	
189	To clean:
190	
191	```sh
192	source ./setup.sh clean         # all four
193	source ./setup.sh clean qemu    # just QEMU build/
194	source ./setup.sh clean vsim
195	source ./setup.sh clean plugin
196	source ./setup.sh clean simpoint
197	```
198	
199	### 1.5 Build the test fixtures (RISC-V ELFs)
200	
201	Fixtures are small RISC-V programs that exercise specific transport
202	paths. They are NOT built by `setup.sh`; build them once:
203	
204	```sh
205	make -C tests/fixtures -j
206	```
207	
208	One fixture at a time:
209	
210	```sh
211	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf
212	```
213	
214	Output ELFs land next to the sources under
215	`tests/fixtures/*.elf`. The fixtures depend on the Andes
216	RISC-V GCC + the `libgloss_vh` semihosting library. The toolchain path
217	comes from `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` (see section 1.3); to override for one
218	invocation:
219	
220	```sh
221	make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain
222	```
223	
224	### 1.6 Sanity check the build
225	
226	```sh
227	# All four artifacts present?
228	ls build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
229	ls verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
230	ls qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
231	ls tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
232	
233	# Smallest possible end-to-end - one CSR-mode round-trip:
234	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 \
235	  bash tests/e2e.sh
236	```
237	
238	Expected last line:
239	
240	```
241	[rt_c_v_regs 3/3 mode=csr] PASS: round-trip exit code 0
242	```
243	
244	If you see `skip: ... not built`, redo `source ./setup.sh` and
245	re-build fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`).
246	
247	---
248	
249	## 2. Configuring the simulator
250	
251	There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
252	vars in 2.1.
253	
254	### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)
255	
256	`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
257	somewhere non-default.
258	
259	| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
260	|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
261	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
262	| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`                 | every harness            |
263	| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
264	| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `verilator/build/sim_*`                  | every harness            |
265	| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
266	| `SIMPOINT_BIN`  | `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`                    | M4/T7 demos              |
267	| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
268	| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (some demos use 120)                        | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
269	| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
270	| `EXPECT_RC`     | 0                                                | expected QEMU2 exit code |
271	| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
272	| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
273	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` | `/dev/shm`                                       | backing dir for `--mmap-size`; redirect when /dev/shm too small |
274	
275	Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:
276	
277	```sh
278	VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
279	  bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
280	```
281	
282	### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML
283	
284	`verilator/config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The
285	default is `ax45mpv_premium`:
286	
287	```yaml
288	cpus:
289	  ax45mpv_premium:
290	    cpu_series: 45
291	    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
292	    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
293	    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
294	    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
295	    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
296	    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
297	```
298	
299	Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML:
300	
301	```sh
302	cd verilator
303	cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
304	cmake --build build -j
305	```
306	
307	`-DVSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID=ON` registers the e2e fixtures with CTest;
308	`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model).
309	
310	### 2.3 QEMU plugin args
311	
312	The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
313	select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:
314	
315	| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
316	|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
317	| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
318	| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | M2: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the CSR-insn matcher.              |
319	| `icount=N`           | M3: drain on the N-th retired insn (per vcpu).                         |
320	| `bbv_out=PATH`       | M4: emit one SimPoint BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.           |
321	| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by M4 and M5). Must be > 0.                      |
322	| `slice_at=K`         | M5: drain at the end of the K-th slice. Requires `slice=N`.            |
323	| `drain_at_exit=1`    | F14: drain when QEMU exits naturally; overrides `minstret` with a plugin-side per-insn counter. Used by `./hsim estimate --icount 0`. |
324	
325	If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (M1): the
326	plugin matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire.
327	
328	Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):
329	
330	```
331	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
332	```
333	
334	Example (icount mode):
335	
336	```
337	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin,icount=10000
338	```
339	
340	### 2.4 vsim CLI flags
341	
342	`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:
343	
344	| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
345	|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
346	| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
347	| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
348	| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
349	| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
350	| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
351	| `--qemu-binary PATH`          | After drain, spawn this QEMU as Phase 3 (QEMU2).        |
352	| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | M2 exit: drain when this PC retires.                    |
353	| `--hybrid-icount N`           | M3 exit: drain after N committed insns (vsim side).     |
354	| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
355	| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |
356	
357	Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
358	`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.
359	
360	Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
361	license-gated and off by default).
362	
363	### 2.5 Requesting more memory (`--mmap-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)
364	
365	By default every `./hsim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
366	a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
367	workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
368	RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:
369	
370	| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
371	|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
372	| `--mmap-size SPEC` | flag on `run`, `profile`, `archive`, `estimate` | request a larger mmap (`SPEC` = `128M`, `8G`, `1.5G`, `2T`, or raw bytes). Default `128M`. |
373	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | override the backing directory (default `/dev/shm`). |
374	
375	Selection rule is deliberately simple: if `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` is set we
376	use it, otherwise `/dev/shm`. We check free space via `statvfs` and
377	error rc=2 with a clear hint if the pinned dir can't hold the request.
378	There is **no fallback chain** -- we never silently switch directories
379	on you.
380	
381	Examples:
382	
383	```sh
384	# Small request; default backend is /dev/shm.
385	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr --mmap-size 256M
386	
387	# 8 GiB request that won't fit /dev/shm: redirect to a disk-backed dir.
388	HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch/hsim \

437	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
438	
439	| ID  | Trigger                                | Where        | When to pick it                                                |
440	|-----|----------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
441	| M1  | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` insn match          | QEMU1 + vsim | Default. Your binary can embed `csrwi` markers.                |
442	| M2  | PC equals an ROI boundary              | QEMU1 + vsim | Any symbol or `0x` address (default: `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`). No CSR markers needed. |
443	| M3  | Retired-instruction count              | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is NOT yours (no CSR/symbol). Use a spin loop / blob.   |
444	| M4  | BBV emit + offline SimPoint cluster    | QEMU1 only   | Phase identification before the real run.                      |
445	| M5  | Drain at end of slice K                | QEMU1        | Replay one cluster representative slice on vsim.               |
446	| M6  | Archive state.bin + mem + meta after drain | orchestrator | Capture a portable, shippable checkpoint.                     |
447	| M7  | Replay a snap/K archive                | orchestrator | Resume the same checkpoint hours / days / hosts later.         |
448	| M8  | QEMU2 exits naturally via semihosting  | QEMU2        | Always. End-of-program signal.                                 |
449	
450	M1/M2/M3 are the three ways to delimit the ROI. M4..M7 stack on top
451	of them for SimPoint-style phase replay. M8 is automatic.
452	
453	Decision flow:
454	
455	```
456	Can you edit the binary?
457	  yes -> insert csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 around the ROI -> M1
458	  no  -> Is there a symbol or PC address at each ROI boundary?
459	           yes -> M2  (--roi-start / --roi-end; defaults to the
460	                  _hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc markers when present)
461	           no  -> Use icount  -> M3
462	You want phase-aware replay?  -> M4 + M5 + M6 + M7   (the T7 demo automates this)
463	```
464	
465	> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (M1/M2):** keep the measured
466	> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
467	> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
468	> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
469	> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
470	> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
471	> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
472	> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

703	### 4.6.5 `./hsim estimate` - SimPoint cycle estimator
704	
705	`./hsim estimate <elf>` runs the full pipeline (M4 BBV profile -> SimPoint
706	cluster -> per-phase QEMU+vsim drain) and aggregates a weighted CPI to
707	project a cycle count for the whole program:
708	
709	```sh
710	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
711	```
712	
713	Default `--icount 0` means **run the program to its natural exit** (e.g.
714	libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT). The plugin counts every retired insn via a
715	per-insn TCG callback and writes that count into the drained state file's
716	`minstret` field; hsim uses it as `N_total` in:
717	
718	```
719	CPI_i           = delta_mcycle_i / vsim_icount
720	weighted_CPI    = sum_i ( w_i * CPI_i )
721	estimated_cycles = N_total * weighted_CPI
722	```
723	
724	Pass `--icount N` (positive) to instead cap the profile pass at N insns
725	and use N as the multiplier (useful for very long-running workloads
726	where you only want to characterize the first N insns).
727	
728	Example output (gemm.elf, ~254K insns):
729	
730	```
731	profile: 4 BBV rows -> .../profile.bb (N_total=254391)
732	cluster: 4 phases
733	phase K=0 w=0.020 delta_mcycle=48105 CPI=9.621
734	phase K=4 w=0.940 delta_mcycle=58621 CPI=11.724
735	...
736	estimated_cycles=2955387  (N=254391, weighted_CPI=11.617)
737	```
738	
739	Caveats:
740	
741	- The fixture must reach `_exit` (return from `main`, or call `exit(0)`).
742	  Programs that hang in an infinite loop will hit the QEMU 30s profile
743	  timeout; pass `--icount N` instead.
744	- The ELF must be linked at the andes_ae350 `-bios` load address
745	  (`0x00100000`); use the linker script `tests/fixtures/test.ld` or the
746	  fixture Makefile. ELFs at other addresses won't execute.
747	
748	#### How to pick `--slice` and `--max-k`
749	
750	These two flags trade profile granularity against vsim cost. Here is the
751	short version; the rest of this section explains why.
752	
753	```
754	slice  ~= N_total / 20         # aim for ~20 BBV rows
755	max-k  =  2                    # start simple, increase only if needed
756	```
757	
758	**Two-step workflow.** First run with defaults to learn N_total, then
759	re-run with a tuned slice:
760	
761	```sh
762	./hsim estimate myprog.elf
763	# read the line:  profile: <rows> BBV rows ... (N_total=<N>)
764	# then:
765	./hsim estimate myprog.elf --slice $((N/20))
766	```
767	
768	**Picking `--slice`** (insns per BBV row). One BBV row is the smallest
769	unit SimPoint can cluster. Too few rows -> k-means cannot find structure.
770	Too many rows -> long profile pass and long clustering. Aim for ~20.
771	
772	| Program size (N_total) | Pick `--slice`  |
773	|------------------------|-----------------|
774	| < 10K (toy)            | 500             |
775	| 10K..100K              | 1000..5000      |
776	| 100K..1M               | 5000..50000     |
777	| > 1M                   | 50000+          |
778	
779	**Picking `--max-k`** (number of phases). Each phase costs **one extra
780	QEMU+vsim drain pair** (~5..10s). SimPoint will sometimes pick fewer
781	phases than `--max-k` if the workload is uniform, so `max-k` is an upper
782	bound, not a fixed count.
783	
784	| Workload structure              | Pick `--max-k` |
785	|---------------------------------|----------------|
786	| Single loop kernel              | 2 (init + body) |
787	| Init + kernel + cleanup         | 3              |
788	| Multi-kernel (e.g. 2 GEMMs)     | 4..6           |
789	| Large benchmark mix             | 8..16          |
790	
791	**Sanity checks after a run.** Read the per-phase rows and apply:
792	
793	1. `BBV rows >= 2 * max_k`. If fewer, drop `--slice` so more rows fit.
794	2. Weights add to ~1.0 and are not all small. If all `--max-k` phases
795	   have similar weights, the workload is uniform and you can drop `max_k`.
796	3. CPIs differ across phases. If every phase reports the same CPI, you
797	   are paying for vsim time without gaining accuracy. Drop `max_k`.
798	
799	**Worked example: gemm.elf** (N_total = 254391):
800	
801	```sh
802	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
803	# Output:
804	# profile: 4 BBV rows -> .../profile.bb (N_total=254391)
805	# phase K=0 w=0.020 ...   phase K=1 w=0.020 ...
806	# phase K=2 w=0.020 ...   phase K=4 w=0.940 CPI=11.724
807	```
808	
809	`slice=5000` gave only 4 BBV rows -- too few for `max_k=4`. The weights
810	also tell you one phase (K=4, the GEMM kernel) accounts for 94% of the
811	program; the other three are startup. A cleaner setup:
812	
813	```sh
814	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 10000 --max-k 2
815	# slice=10000 -> ~25 BBV rows; max_k=2 -> startup + kernel only
816	```
817	
818	**One-line rule.** Start with `--slice $((N_total/20)) --max-k 2`. Raise
819	`max_k` only when a single dominant phase (w > 0.8) hides sub-phase
820	detail you care about.

3	## Goal

5	Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on

12	## Why two builds of one source
13	
14	`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
15	matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
16	marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:
17	
18	- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
19	- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

21	Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

23	### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
24	- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
25	  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: every switching mode (M1-M8) the repo ships, with copy-paste
6	commands and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across three phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim  --(state file + same mmap)-->  QEMU2
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)                       (fast)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN each leg drains its
20	state and hands off. The codebase ships eight rules (M1-M8). They
21	plug into the same harness; you pick the rule with plugin args and
22	vsim CLI flags. The fixture binary does NOT need to change between
23	rules (one fixture can be driven by several modes).
24	
25	This document teaches one mode at a time, then exercises that
26	combine modes.
27	
28	### Quick map
29	
30	| ID | Name                           | Drain trigger                                   | Used at        |
31	|----|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------|
32	| M1 | CSR insn match (default)       | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) | QEMU1, vsim    |
33	| M2 | PC / ROI resolve               | PC equals an ROI boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (default `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`) | QEMU1, vsim    |
34	| M3 | icount                         | N retired instructions                          | QEMU1, vsim    |
35	| M4 | BBV profile + SimPoint cluster | Plugin emits 1 row per slice; offline clustering | QEMU1 + tool   |
36	| M5 | slice-consume                  | End of slice index K                             | QEMU1          |
37	| M6 | archive emit                   | After drain, write `snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` | orchestrator |
38	| M7 | checkpoint replay              | Hydrate `snap/K/` into a fresh mmap, resume      | orchestrator   |
39	| M8 | end-of-program                 | QEMU2 exits via semihosting `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED`  | QEMU2          |
40	
41	M1/M2/M3 are entry/exit triggers (the "boundary" question).
42	M4/M5/M6/M7 are pipeline stages for the full SimPoint flow.
43	M8 is the natural end-of-run signal (always at the tail).
44	
45	---
46	
47	## 1. One-time prerequisites
48	
49	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
50	
51	```sh
52	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
53	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
54	```
55	
56	You should now have:
57	
58	| Artifact                                  | Purpose                           |
59	|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
60	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`          | QEMU binary (phase 1 and phase 3) |
61	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
62	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`        | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
63	| `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`             | SimPoint clustering tool (M4)     |
64	| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`           | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_regs)  |
65	
66	Common env vars (auto-detected by every demo; override only if you
67	keep these elsewhere):
68	
69	```sh
70	export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
71	export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
72	export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
73	```
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 2. M1 + M8 - CSR insn match (the default path)
78	
79	### What it does
80	
81	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire
82	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
83	same on `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes
84	ax45mp, so the fixture binary embeds these two `csrwi` instructions
85	at the ROI boundaries.
86	
87	M8 is automatic: after vsim hands back, QEMU2 finishes the workload
88	and exits via `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED` semihosting.
89	
90	### Inputs
91	
92	- Fixture ELF with `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` in its source.
93	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
94	
95	### Output
96	
97	- Phase-by-phase log line + final `exit 0`.
98	
99	### Run it
100	
101	```sh
102	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
103	bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
104	```
105	
106	Expected last line:
107	
108	```
109	[demo M1] PASS (CSR insn match (M1+M8))
110	```
111	
112	### Drill-down (what the demo does internally)
113	
114	Inside, the demo calls the generic harness:
115	
116	```sh
117	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 \
118	  bash tests/e2e.sh
119	```
120	
121	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the
122	M1 default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
123	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`
124	PCs at retire.
125	
126	### Exercise 1
127	
128	Switch fixture from `rt_c_v_regs` to `rt_c_matmul`. The script is
129	fixture-parameterized:
130	
131	```sh
132	FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 \
133	  bash tests/e2e.sh
134	```
135	
136	Verify the last line says `PASS: round-trip exit code 0`. Then read
137	`tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.c` and confirm where the two
138	`csrwi 0x7C0, *` markers live (`enter_vsim()` / `exit_vsim()` helpers).
139	
140	---
141	
142	## 3. M2 - PC symbol resolve
143	
144	### What it does
145	
146	Same round-trip as M1 but the trigger is a PC value (not an opcode
147	match). The harness resolves each ROI boundary - taken from
148	`ROI_START` / `ROI_END`, which default to the symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc`
149	and `_hybrid_exit_pc` - to an address (a `0x` value is used verbatim; a
150	name is looked up with `nm`), then passes:
151	
152	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
153	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
154	
155	CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions in
156	the binary become inert (CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor-defined write).
157	
158	This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source: point the ROI
159	at any function or address the binary already has.
160	
161	### Inputs
162	
163	- Same fixture as M1 (`rt_c_v_regs`). With the defaults, the ELF must
164	  define `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` (the C-level fixtures all
165	  do). To target a different region, set `ROI_START` / `ROI_END` (or
166	  `./hsim run --roi-start/--roi-end`) to any symbol or `0x` address - then
167	  no marker symbols are needed at all.
168	
169	### Output
170	
171	- `exit 0`, last log line `[demo M2] PASS`.
172	
173	### Run it
174	
175	```sh
176	bash tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh
177	```
178	
179	### Drill-down
180	
181	```sh
182	ENTER_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
183	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
184	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
185	EXIT_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
186	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
187	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
188	
189	# QEMU plugin arg
190	... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC
191	
192	# vsim arg
193	... --hybrid-exit-pc 0x$EXIT_PC
194	```
195	
196	### Exercise 2
197	
198	Compare exit values: run the demo with TRIGGER_MODE=csr and again
199	with TRIGGER_MODE=pc on the same fixture. Both must exit 0 and
200	both must drain the same PC. Use:
201	
202	```sh
203	xxd state_csr.bin | head -4
204	xxd state_pc.bin  | head -4
205	```
206	
207	The PC field is at offset 16 (`hybrid_state_v1::pc`). For most
208	fixtures `pc(csr) == pc(pc)` because both modes drain right after
209	the entry trigger retires.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## 4. M3 - icount round-trip
214	
215	### What it does
216	
217	Both legs drain on retired-instruction count alone. No CSR, no PC
218	symbol. Suitable for CSR-less workloads (an infinite spin loop, a
219	benchmark you cannot edit, etc.).
220	
221	- QEMU plugin: `icount=N1` -> drain at the N1-th retired insn
222	- vsim: `--hybrid-icount N2` -> drain N2 insns after resume
223	
224	### Inputs
225	
226	- Any ELF; `icount_spin.elf` is the canonical CSR-less fixture.
227	
228	### Output
229	
230	- Both QEMU1 and vsim exit 200 with a non-empty state file. There is
231	  no QEMU2 phase because `icount_spin` spins forever (no natural
232	  semihosting exit).
233	
234	### Run it
235	
236	```sh
237	bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
238	```
239	
240	Override targets:
241	
242	```sh
243	QEMU_ICOUNT=20000 VSIM_ICOUNT=8000 \
244	  bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
245	```
246	
247	### Exercise 3
248	
249	Predict where the drained PC will land for `icount_spin.elf`. The
250	loop body has two RVC instructions at PCs `0x100002` and `0x100004`.
251	Run with VSIM_ICOUNT=5000. The drained PC should be one of those
252	two values. Read the demo's `read_u64` helper to confirm how the PC
253	is extracted from the state file (offset 16, little-endian 8 bytes).
254	
255	---
256	
257	## 5. M4 - BBV profile + SimPoint cluster
258	
259	### What it does
260	
261	QEMU plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector (BBV) row per slice of N
262	retired insns. The output is a SimPoint `.bb` file. Offline,
263	`tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads it and clusters the rows into K
264	representative phases.
265	
266	This is the SimPoint "profile" pass. It produces:
267	
268	- `simpts` file: 1 line per cluster, `<slice_idx> <cluster_id>`
269	- `weights` file: 1 line per cluster, `<weight> <cluster_id>`
270	
271	Later, M5+M6+M7 replay just those representative slices.
272	
273	### Inputs
274	
275	- Any ELF. CSR-less or not - the plugin emits BBV rows regardless.
276	
277	### Output
278	
279	- `WORKDIR/<elf>.bb`, `WORKDIR/simpts`, `WORKDIR/weights` persist on
280	  disk so that M5/M7 can consume them.
281	
282	### Run it
283	
284	```sh
285	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile \
286	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
287	```
288	
289	Override the slice and total count:
290	
291	```sh
292	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-bigger SLICE=2000 ICOUNT=20000 MAXK=4 \
293	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
294	```
295	
296	Expected rows = `ICOUNT / SLICE`. The demo asserts this.
297	
298	### Drill-down: plugin args
299	
300	```
301	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,\
302	        outfile=$STATE,\
303	        bbv_out=$WORKDIR/profile.bb,\
304	        slice=1000,\
305	        icount=10000
306	```
307	
308	`slice` is shared with M5; `bbv_out=` is what activates emit mode.
309	
310	### Exercise 4
311	
312	Run the demo with WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-ex SLICE=500 ICOUNT=10000 MAXK=3.
313	Inspect `simpts` and `weights`. The number of lines in each file
314	must be equal and at most `MAXK`. Sum the first column of `weights`
315	- it should be approximately 1.0 (SimPoint may emit unnormalised on
316	small inputs; the demo prints this sum for sanity-check).
317	
318	---
319	
320	## 6. M5 - slice-consume entry
321	
322	### What it does
323	
324	QEMU plugin drains at the end of slice K (0-based), where each slice
325	is N retired insns. This is the SimPoint "replay" entry: you ran M4
326	once, picked phase K, and now you want vsim to start from the END of
327	slice K (the QEMU drain leaves you with exactly that architectural
328	state).
329	
330	Plugin args:
331	
332	- `slice=N` (insns per slice; SAME N as the profile pass)
333	- `slice_at=K` (drain at the end of the K-th slice, 0-based)
334	- `icount=M` (safety fallback - if K is invalid, drain at M anyway)
335	
336	### Inputs
337	
338	- Same ELF as the profile pass. Same `slice=N`.
339	- K from `simpts` (T4 output) OR from env `SLICE_AT`.
340	
341	### Output
342	
343	- State file drained at the slice boundary. PC inside the ROI.
344	
345	### Run it
346	
347	Using M4's output directly:
348	
349	```sh
350	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
351	SIMPTS=/tmp/m4-profile/simpts \
352	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
353	```
354	
355	Manual K choice:
356	
357	```sh
358	SLICE=1000 SLICE_AT=3 \
359	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
360	```
361	
362	Inside, the demo combines two modes: M5 for entry (QEMU side) and
363	M3 for exit (vsim side, `--hybrid-icount`). They are independent;
364	each side picks its own mode.
365	
366	### Exercise 5
367	
368	Pipeline M4 -> M5 by hand (no demo script):
369	
370	1. Run M4 with `SLICE=1000 ICOUNT=10000 MAXK=2`. Note `WORKDIR`.
371	2. `cat $WORKDIR/simpts` and pick the first cluster's slice index, K.
372	3. Run vsim manually:
373	   - QEMU plugin `slice=1000,slice_at=K,outfile=...`
374	   - vsim `--resume-from-qemu STATE --hybrid-icount 5000 --handoff-out STATE_V`
375	4. Confirm both legs exit 200.
376	
377	This is exactly what `demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh` automates.
378	
379	---
380	
381	## 7. M6 + M7 - archive emit and checkpoint replay
382	
383	### What it does
384	
385	M6 packages a drained state plus its shared mmap into a portable
386	archive directory:
387	
388	```
389	snap/K/
390	  state.bin    # hybrid_state_v1 (8.5 KB)
391	  mem          # full shared mmap (128 MB by default)
392	  meta.json    # schema=1, abi_version=1, mmap_size, slice_index, etc.

1	# Hybrid Simulator: QEMU + Verilator (vsim)
2	
3	A plan to extend `vsim` from a pure Verilator cycle-accurate simulator into a hybrid functional/RTL simulator that runs the boring code in QEMU at MHz speed and switches into Verilator only for the cycle-accurate region of interest (ROI), then optionally hands back.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Context
8	
9	`vsim` runs at 5-9 KHz on Andes RISC-V cores. A typical workload spends >99% of cycles in boot, libc init, and warm-up before reaching the kernel under study. Today the only escape hatch is `--save`/`--continue`, which still requires an initial RTL run to reach the snapshot point. There is also already a `--kanata-loop-{start,end,skip,record}` mechanism (`src/main.cpp:183-214`) that identifies the interesting loop iterations.
10	
11	We want: run everything before the ROI in QEMU (functional, MHz), hand the architectural state to Verilator at the ROI boundary, run the ROI cycle-accurately to record kanata/clarity pipeline data, and optionally hand back to QEMU to finish.
12	
13	The intended outcome: 100x-1000x reduction in wall-clock time for benchmarking workflows that only care about steady-state pipeline behavior of a small kernel, with byte-identical kanata output for the recorded window vs. a fully-RTL baseline.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 2. Tutorial: Why This Is Technically Feasible
18	
19	### 2.1 The state-exchange problem, reframed
20	
21	A naive hybrid sim has to "transfer" CPU state between two simulators. In practice the state splits into three categories with very different costs:
22	
23	| Category | Items | Size | Strategy |
24	|---|---|---|---|
25	| Architectural regs | x0..x31, f0..f31, V regs, key CSRs | 4-8 KB | **Copy** via well-defined ABI struct |
26	| Memory | guest RAM, ILM/DLM | MB-GB | **Share** via `mmap` - zero copy |
27	| Microarchitectural state | TLB, caches, BPU, store buffer | KB-MB | **Discard** - let cold starts repopulate |
28	
29	The key trick: **memory does not move**. QEMU runs with `-object memory-backend-file,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/vsim-ram`. vsim's `SimpleMemory::data` (`src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:20`) is changed to an `mmap` of the same fd. Both simulators read and write the same physical bytes. The same trick is used by QEMU's CPR (`docs/devel/migration/CPR.rst`) and gem5's `SimpleSwitchableProcessor`. RAM size becomes irrelevant.
30	
31	Microarch state is intentionally discarded. We accept cold caches/BPU on entry into Verilator and rely on the existing `kanata_loop_skip N` mechanism to warm them up before recording. This matches the gem5 "switch + warmup" pattern.
32	
33	### 2.2 The trigger: a magic CSR convention
34	
35	We need both sides to agree on "the ROI starts here." Reuse the user-defined CSR space at `0x7C0`:
36	
37	```asm
38	csrwi 0x7C0, 0   # enter detail (QEMU -> vsim)
39	csrwi 0x7C0, 1   # exit detail  (vsim -> QEMU)
40	```
41	
42	- **QEMU** sees this via a TCG plugin: `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_insn_exec_cb()` with a per-instruction filter that pattern-matches the encoding of `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` (mask `0xfff03073` against the 32-bit insn). On hit, the plugin drains state and exits.
43	- **vsim** sees this via the existing retire signal taps in `src/signals/common_signals_45.hpp`. We pre-scan the ELF for PCs containing `csrw 0x7C0, *` (LIEF is already linked - `src/utils/elf_loader.hpp`), then watch for retire-of-PC against that set.
44	
45	Phase 4 lifts this further: `--kanata-loop-start <pc>` and `--kanata-loop-end <pc>` already specify the ROI by PC. The orchestrator wraps these as PC-trigger events and **the binary needs no magic CSR at all**.
46	
47	We deliberately avoid `tohost`/`fromhost` (HTIF reserved) and `ecall` (already used by the runtime).
48	
49	### 2.3 The write-back path: existing JTAG/DTM, in-process
50	
51	This is the highest-leverage finding. vsim already has:
52	
53	- `src/platform/jtag_dtm.hpp` - a full JTAG DTM implementation with the RISC-V Debug Module
54	- `--jtag-port` CLI flag and OpenOCD support (`src/main.cpp:148-154`)
55	
56	The RISC-V Debug Spec gives Abstract Commands that read/write GPRs (`regno` 0x1000-0x101F), FPRs (0x1020-0x103F), and CSRs (0x0000-0x0FFF) directly via the Debug Module. **Writing all 32 GPRs + 32 FPRs + ~20 critical CSRs is ~85 DMI transactions**, which is ~hundreds of cycles - negligible compared to the millions of cycles we save.
57	
58	We drive the DTM **in-process**, calling its `handle_dmi_*` methods directly without an OpenOCD socket. No DPI shim, no Verilog modifications, no per-CPU-variant code (works for all ten CPU wrappers in `src/cpu_wrappers/`).
59	
60	The sequence to "resume from QEMU state":
61	
62	1. Reset CPU; halt request via DM
63	2. For each register in the ABI struct, issue Abstract Command (`regno` + data)
64	3. Set DPC = saved PC
65	4. Issue `dret` via Program Buffer
66	
67	Vector registers are moved via a Program Buffer `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` sweep against a guest-RAM scratch region (implemented in Phase 5; see `pb_v_data_sweep`). CPU-specific custom CSRs the DM cannot reach via Abstract Commands use the Program Buffer `csrrw` fallback (`write_csr_abstract_or_pb`); last resort is an mmap-shared mirror via DPI.
68	
69	### 2.4 The QEMU side: a TCG plugin against the existing build
70	
71	`/local/nick/qemu_v5/build/qemu-system-riscv64` is QEMU **9.2.0** (verified). This is recent enough for the full plugin API:
72	
73	- `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_insn_exec_cb()` - per-insn callback
74	- `qemu_plugin_get_registers()` / `qemu_plugin_read_register()` - drain GPR/FP/CSR
75	- `qemu_plugin_request_exit()` - stop QEMU cleanly
76	
77	Templates already on disk: `/local/nick/qemu_v5/contrib/plugins/{execlog.c, hotblocks.c, bbv.c}`. We add one new plugin `hybrid_handoff.c` next to them. No QEMU patches, no fork.
78	
79	### 2.5 What does NOT work and is out of scope
80	
81	- **MMIO inside the ROI**: device state lives in QEMU C and has no mirror in RTL. Document; fail loudly via an interconnect watch in Phase 5.
82	- **lr/sc reservations across handoff**: invalidate at handoff; do not transfer.
83	- **Self-modifying code in the ROI**: the magic CSR is a synchronization boundary by convention.
84	- **mcycle/minstret continuity**: monotonic across handoffs but not equal to a fully-RTL run; documented discontinuity.
85	- **Andes-internal QEMU fork** (`andescycle-dev-v0.16-17-g03dfe23.tar.gz`): treated as opaque. Plan against mainline QEMU 9.2.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 3. Architecture at a Glance
90	
91	```
92	                              shared mmap RAM (/dev/shm/vsim-ram)
93	                                           |
94	              +----------------------------+----------------------------+
95	              |                                                         |
96	              v                                                         v
97	       QEMU 9.2.0 + plugin                                    vsim (SystemC + Verilator)
98	       +---------------------+                                +-----------------------+
99	       | TCG insn loop       |     state.bin (ABI struct)     | SystemC main loop     |
100	       | hybrid_handoff.so   |  <-->  [ABI v1 packed]   <-->  | jtag_dtm in-process   |
101	       | csrw 0x7C0 -> drain |                                | csr_trigger -> drain  |
102	       +---------------------+                                +-----------------------+
103	              ^                                                         ^
104	              |                                                         |
105	              +--orchestrator script (vsim-hybrid)----------------------+
106	                  enter-pc / exit-pc mode also supported
